create.title: Exact squarefree lcm and gcd-lift compression with target-safe exact phase classes
create.statement_tex: Let R=X^(1/4), N=floor(X), DE asymp M<=R^2, D<=sqrt(M), Q=2sqrt(ND/E), and retain every exact Round-148 prefix. For squarefree d put d_o=d/(d,2). Summing the odd squarefree Mobius cells with lcm n gives C_d(n)=mu(u)mu(v) exactly for n=uv^2, u|d_o, mu^2(uv)=1, (v,d)=1, u,v odd, and zero otherwise; at odd p|d_o the exponent-two cells cancel and p=2 is absent. With the literal nonempty-progression indicator kappa_(d,U), write ell=gL, q=gq_0, (L,q_0)=1 and B_(d,U)(L)=sum_g C_d(gL)kappa_(d,U)(gL)/g. Then T=sum_d mu^2(d)(D/d)G_U(d), where G_U(d)=sum_((L,q_0)=1,q_0 asymp LQ) chi_4(Lq_0)B_(d,U)(L)W_(d,U)(L/q_0)e(NdL/q_0)/L. Uniformly for every finite prefix, sum_L |B_(d,U)(L)|^2/L+sum_L |B_(d,U)(L)|/L<<X^epsilon. The literal equal-cell energy is <<DQX^epsilon. Distinct exact N-alignments have energy <<DX^epsilon, and all exact phase classes including the literal diagonal have energy <<DQX^epsilon, hence are target-safe because Q<=R^2. The nonexact moving-coefficient near/generic energy and the RD scalar target remain open.
create.next_action: Prove the nonexact moving-coefficient near/generic correlation with the actual B_(d,U), profiles, prefixes, chi_4 signs, common divisors, and every aspect, or perform a complete Euler recombination that produces a source-legal signed family.

create.title: Moving-coefficient gcd-lift near-collision and fixed-vector source obstruction
create.statement_tex: After the exact gcd-lift compression, the prefix-uniform lift norm, literal DQ diagonal, every exact N-alignment, q_0|N, and the reduced-denominator stratum q_*=q_0/(q_0,N)<=R are target-safe. For two nonexact cells write q_(0,i)=hr_i, (r_1,r_2)=1, delta=L_1r_2-L_2r_1, and rho=Ndelta-khr_1r_2 with |rho|<=hr_1r_2/2. The first open collar is 0<|rho|<=hr_1r_2/D. Its d-kernel contains mu^2(d)B_(d,U)(L_1)conj(B_(d,U)(L_2)) and both moving profiles and exact prefixes. Montgomery--Vaughan's primal and dual large sieves require one common coefficient vector and do not apply verbatim. The audited squarefree-progression, inverse-square, Kloosterman-fraction, and partially fixed-modulus dispersion theorems have different coefficients, phases, averages, diagonals, separability, or ranges. Even an illegal fixed-vector unwrapped-spacing diagnostic has capacity Q(D+M)X^epsilon and loses sqrt(M) in energy. This is a source-applicability and proof-placement no-go, not a lower bound for the signed row and not an impossibility theorem for a coefficient-sensitive correlation or further exact recombination.

reject.reason: Only alpha,b,ell,q and the gcd-lift variables are odd. For squarefree even d, the lcm coefficient depends on d_o=d/(d,2), and p=2 contributes no local factor.
At every odd p|d_o, the two exponent-two Mobius cells have signs -1 and +1 and cancel exactly.
The closed cube-free lift formula and absolute Euler majorants use only 0<=kappa<=1 and finite support; arbitrary irregular prefixes satisfy the same norm.
The norm controls only the literal diagonal. The nonexact near/generic Gram matrix retains a genuinely d-dependent arithmetic coefficient and moving profile.
After exact lcm and gcd-lift compression, the literal diagonal is DQX^epsilon<=R^2DX^epsilon. The Round-148 loss was specific to unrecombined progression cells.
Distinct cells can have the same NL/q_0 phase modulo one. They are classified by common factors or reduced phase classes and are target-safe, not absent.
The distinct exact off-diagonal is O(DX^epsilon), and all exact phase classes including the literal diagonal are O(DQX^epsilon). The first open sector is nonexact.
Montgomery--Vaughan Theorem 1 and its duality lemma retain one common coefficient vector. The literal B_(d,U) profile is a matrix, not that vector.
Their printed reduced-modulus ranges lie inside q_*<=D<=R, an elementary target-safe stratum, and their coefficients and averages also differ.
Those theorems require independent sequences and inverse-fraction or fixed-residue convolution structure; the Round-149 coefficient is jointly determined by d,L,q_0,prefix and profile.
The Q(D+M) and raw rational-spacing losses are upper capacities of illegal fixed-vector or positive-spacing placements, not lower bounds for the actual signed energy.
The nonexact moving-row energy, signed t=1 scalar, every t>=2 layer, cross owner, remaining M1 and M2 owners, endpoint, M9, bridge, and quarter target remain open.
